persistent_identifier_status: Repository-local identifier for this transcription; the DOI identifies the source article, not this derived dataset.
title: Pre-ensiling wilted Italian ryegrass properties at two dry-matter targets
citation: Assis, J. A., Carbonare, M. S. D., & Schmidt, P. (2026). Different dry matter contents on the fermentation and preservation of wilted ryegrass silage with or without microbial inoculants. Revista Brasileira de Zootecnia, 55. https://doi.org/10.37496/rbz5520250112
source_locations: Methods sections 2.1–2.2 for sampling and analysis basis
geography: Forage grown at a commercial farm in Castro, Paraná, Brazil; research performed by UFPR in Curitiba, Paraná, Brazil.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated on the article page. Cite the article and retain the license attribution.
material_scope: Wilted Italian ryegrass (Lolium multiflorum L., cultivar F ABC 1), sampled at harvest targets of 32% and 45% dry matter before ensiling. This is cultivated livestock forage, not Dutch roadside grass.
experimental_conditions: The crop was manually cut on 2021-08-20 and field-wilted for 24 h (32% DM target) or 48 h (45% DM target), turned three times daily, then chopped to 10 mm. The harvested forage was sampled in duplicate. Table 1 reports one value per harvest and no standard deviation.
data_scope: Fourteen Table 1 properties are transcribed. The two DM measurements retain their separate oven temperatures; chemical concentrations retain the source DM basis; microbial counts retain log10 CFU/g and the source does not further specify the mass basis in the table.
table_layout: One row per reported property; separate columns retain the two harvest DM targets as presented in Table 1. This table-native layout is a raw reference transcription, not a normalized runtime parameter table.
limitations: Reference-only; no GreenHub runtime parameter or default is mapped to these observations.
The feed is cultivated Italian ryegrass in Brazil, not Dutch roadside grass or the project-specific VARTA feedstock.
Table 1 reports a single value per harvest. Duplicate sampling is reported in Methods, but no biological replicate count, standard deviation, or raw replicate observations are provided in the table.
The two DM columns are target harvest groups, not a continuous moisture response curve.
Crude protein and fiber values are source-specific forage composition, not a measured composition of protein-recovery residuals.
conversion_or_processing: Values and units were transcribed from Table 1 without numeric conversion, averaging, imputation, interpolation, or activation. The source distinguishes 60 °C and 105 °C dry-matter analyses; these are retained as different properties.
uncertainty: No standard deviations are reported in Table 1. Duplicate sampling is noted but is not interpreted as independent biological replication.
